svg.title: How your Fandex Score works
svg.desc: One number per title: the rating you would probably give, times ten. It starts from your average for the medium. Each facet moves it by how you rated the titles that carry it, and the sum is scaled to match the ratings you gave.
svg.text: How your Fandex Score works
One number on every title: what you would probably rate it, times ten. A 72 means about a 7.
It is right to about a point, not a tenth. Nothing here reads the crowd's ratings or what is popular.
1 · WHAT A TITLE IS MADE OF
Fandex breaks every film, show, game or book into its facets:
Platform tags ("PC", "PS5") and noise never count. Where a tag came from counts too:
a provider's theme and a crowd's voted tag (Steam) in full, a genre and an editor's keyword half.
2 · YOUR AVERAGE FOR THE MEDIUM IS WHERE IT STARTS
You rate games 7.3 and films 6.4? A game starts at 73 and a film at 64.
A title the facets say nothing about reads as your average.
Below ten ratings in a medium it starts from your overall average instead.
3 · EACH FACET MOVES IT BY HOW YOU RATED IT
For every facet on the title: your average rating for the titles you rated that carry it,
against your overall average. Only ratings you typed yourself count.
A facet you met once barely moves it; one you met forty times moves it fully.
Games you rate higher than films? That gap is taken out before a facet learns.
Steampunk · you rate it 7.6 over 41 titles · usual 6.7 · +0.9
Disease · you rate it 8.5 over 11 titles · +1.5
Musical · you rate it 4.8 over 9 titles · −1.6
Only the strongest few of each kind count:
The rest are still shown in the breakdown, greyed, with the value they would have had.
Some kinds weigh more: a developer counts twice a tag; cast and writers count nothing
(measured: they predicted nothing).
4 · THE SUM IS SCALED SO THE NUMBER MATCHES WHAT YOU GAVE
The facets' sum is multiplied by a gain fitted to your own ratings, by least squares, so that the score
divided by ten lands on the rating you gave for titles you rated.
A sum below zero has its own gain: it predicts more strongly.
The result is bent near 0 and 100 so it never passes them.
What it said · what the owner gave, 2026-10-27
Right within one point of the rating about 4 times in 10 on films
(guessing the average: 4 in 10 too, a little worse), within two points 3 times in 4.
5 · A TITLE YOU RATED NEVER QUOTES ITSELF
A title you rated is scored as if you had not: its own rating is left out of your average
and of every facet it carries.
That is also how the score checks itself: every rated title against what you gave, on your own device,
and the Why sheet says how right it has been.
6 · HOW OFTEN YOU PICK THIS, SAID BESIDE THE NUMBER
A second question, asked of every facet: how much more often you pick it than average, against ordinary
titles drawn at random, all facets weighed together.
A tag that only rides along (firefighter, on anime films) gets no credit.
It reads as one line, "You pick films like this 3 times more often than average",
and it never moves the number: on titles you rated it read high almost by construction
and made the number worse, so it was taken out (2026-10-27).
Steampunk · 4 times more often than average · 46 of yours
7 · THE COLOUR
Green: at least 4 points above your average for the medium (you would give it about half a point
more than usual). Orange: at least 4 below. Grey: about your usual.
Home's Recommended rail carries green titles only.
WHAT NEVER COUNTS
· the crowd's ratings
· how popular a title is
· when it came out
· episodes watched or hours played
· your rating of the title being scored
· how often you pick it
Only the ratings you typed yourself.
HOW WE CHECK IT
Every change is measured first, per medium:
· how far the score ÷ 10 sits from the rating given,
against guessing the average
· what each band of the score meant
· whether a green badge earns an 8 more often
The goalpost chart on the telemetry page is the running proof.
Fandex Score, version 4 · 2026-10-27 · this picture changes whenever the score does
